items.title: Public trustee regime and Tata Trusts: An old law, a contemporary question
items.summary: When charitable trusts control a substantial stake in a major commercial enterprise, who should determine how that voting power is exercised? The question has acquired renewed significance in the dispute over Tata Sons’ proposed listing, where disagreements within the Tata Trusts have brought fiduciary obligations, boardroom independence and corporate control into sharp focus. India once addressed a related concern through the erstwhile Section 187B of the Companies Act, 1956 (the “1956 Act”), which has since been replaced by the Companies Act, 2013 (the “2013 Act”). Inserted by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 1963 with effect from January 1, 1964, the provision transferred voting rights attached to certain trust-held shares from trustees to a government-appointed Public Trustee. It sought to prevent voting power held through trusts from advancing private interests but did so without requiring an individual finding of misconduct. items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes FIR against persons who put up posters terming Supreme Court judgment a "denial of justice"
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed a criminal case registered against 13 people for allegedly putting up posters in Mangaluru describing a Supreme Court judgment as a “denial of justice" and calling on people to raise their voices for justice [ Mahammed Hanif & others Vs State of Karnataka ]. Justice HP Sandesh held that the slogans amounted to an expression of dissent against the judgment, which fell within the limits of the freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under the Constitution of India. "The same is dissent about the judgment and the same is not in the term of creating disharmony and only it is stated that justice is denied and raise voice and the same is within the scope of Articles 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India," the Court's October 15 ruling said. The Court concluded that such slogans did not attract the cited criminal offences under Sections 153A (promoting enmity) and 295A (deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
